'ddflow --version' takes ~1.0 s and importing ddflow.surfaces.cli ~0.83 s (ddflow.api imports dominate), 'ddflow list/show' ~4.7 s on this loaded machine, so argcomplete-style per-TAB invocation would add 1-5 s per keypress. The derived index .ddflow/index.db-<code fingerprint> is plain sqlite: items(id,kind,title,state,needs,tags,...) 3488 rows, count query 0.0 s, openable read-only with stdlib sqlite3. data.claim: Yes, but narrower than 'merge lanes'. (1) The lock/time saving comes from sharing the gate RUN, which P-batch-gates already designs and decided (D-BG-1..10: one CI/unit_tests/standards run on the merge of path-disjoint members, line-sized reviews, ddmin culprit search, one-transaction fan-out); uniting two agents does not by itself cut suite-lock contention. (2) The new value is freeing the LANE: when the remaining gates are machine gates (ci, unit_tests, standards via roborev) the agent need not wait at all, so release-at-enqueue plus a deterministic integrator frees the lane with no context transfer; only agent-judgement gates (rubber_duck, critic, bug_hunt, dedupe) need an agent, and there one surviving lane can review a combined unit while the donor's context travels as a handoff capsule. (3) ddflow wait cannot be interrupted today in the needed way: it is a blocking log poll, the holder is told at heartbeat, release or complete and never interrupted (services/waits.py), an MCP wait gives no progress and was aborted at 1800 s (Bfc43dae5b9), --max-s is ignored (B-wait-lease-max-s-ignored), and a message to a busy agent is delivered only at its next tool round. The pieces exist: DX-watch-job (done) gives bounded waits with resume tokens that renew leases; a wake reason (ready, merge_offer, yield, message) and an inbox are the missing part.
